outcome: No composite satisfying 2^(c-1) ≡ 1 (mod c^2) — a base-2 Wieferich pseudoprime — has been found or ruled out since 26 January 2024; the question remains exactly as open as it was, and no new bound-moving search targeting this specific composite question was found.
summary: This bullet asks whether any composite c exists with 2^(c-1) ≡ 1 (mod c^2), i.e. a base-2 Wieferich pseudoprime (WPSP). A necessary condition for such a c is that every prime factor of c be a Wieferich prime (p with p^2 | 2^(p-1) - 1), and only two Wieferich primes are known — 1093 and 3511 — with the search for a third completed by PrimeGrid up to 2^64 (~1.8×10^19) as of 29 December 2022, a date before the frozen revision and with no announced continuation. Because the pool of eligible prime factors has not grown and no dedicated computational search of composites (as opposed to primes) for this exact congruence was found reported anywhere in 2024–2026, the question sits precisely where it did in January 2024. I searched broadly for 'Wieferich pseudoprime' work in 2024–2026 and found only unrelated papers: Wieferich primes for Drinfeld modules/function fields (arXiv:2412.11588, arXiv:2512.08060), Wieferich primes in number fields tied to the Ankeny–Artin–Chowla and Mordell conjectures (arXiv:2508.08472), and non-Wieferich prime ideals related to an Erdős conjecture (arXiv:2601.12753) — all of these are analogues over different algebraic objects (function fields, number fields, prime ideals) and change nothing about the classical composite existence question stated in this bullet, so per §3.1 they are related problems, not cases of it, and do not move the status. The current Wikipedia 'Wieferich prime' article's pseudoprime discussion and the OEIS pages A077816 (Wieferich numbers, both prime and composite terms satisfying a related condition, maintained by Max Alekseyev) and A182297 were also checked; neither shows any new composite discovery or new targeted search bound for this specific congruence since 2024. No AI system was mentioned in connection with any of this. I judge this a well-evidenced 'nothing happened' rather than an under-researched null result.
competing_reading: One could argue the PrimeGrid Wieferich-prime search (finished Dec 2022, ruling out a third Wieferich prime below 2^64) is itself relevant 'progress' by narrowing where a composite WPSP's prime factors could live, but that search predates the frozen revision's window and was not extended afterward, so it cannot be used to justify anything other than open/open_stale, and it was already reflected in the pre-2024 state of knowledge that the Wikipedia list captured.
what_would_settle_it: Either an explicit composite c verified (by hand or computer algebra) to satisfy 2^(c-1) ≡ 1 (mod c^2), or a new dedicated computational search (post-January-2024) of composites — not just primes — up to some large bound reported as extending the known search space, or a proof of non-existence.
